## Beta — Hold, resume and resync

Let other automations coexist with the schedule: pause an entity (manual override, open window, away) and hand it back to the schedule when the pause ends. Generic: it works with any service that targets entities, nothing is specific to `climate`. No change to the rule format; all of this is optional.

- **`chronotask.hold`** — pause one or more entities for N minutes, until a date/time, or without expiry (`reason` is free text). Rules do not touch held entities (if a rule targets several, only the held ones are skipped). A new hold replaces the previous one; timed holds resume automatically. Holds are persistent across restarts.
- **`chronotask.resume`** — remove the hold and, with `apply` (default), run the action of the **current state**: the last past event among the enabled rules that target the entity (start or end of a slot; overnight slots, explicit end days and slots without an end are handled). Returns what was applied. Entities that are `unavailable`/`unknown` are skipped with a warning, no retry.
- **`chronotask.resync`** — apply the current state to every entity that is not held (or only the ones given). Never called automatically: call it from an automation after Home Assistant starts or after enabling rules.
- **Sensor attribute `entities`** on `sensor.<planner>_rules`: for each targeted entity `scheduled`, `rule`, `since`, `expected_service`, `expected_data`, `next_change`, `hold`, `hold_until`, `hold_reason` — updated *before* the service is called, so automations can tell a manual change from a ChronoTask action. `capabilities.hold` is `true`.
- **Event `chronotask_action`** on every action (`start`, `end`, `resume`, `resync`), with the same context as the service call.
- `rules` and `entities` are no longer stored in the recorder history.
- Holds that expired while Home Assistant was off are removed at startup without applying anything.
- Internals: pure state logic in `slots.py` and a `tests/` folder (no Home Assistant needed).

Rules targeting areas or devices instead of entities cannot be held. See the README ("Hold, resume and resync") for details and the attribute layout.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/andker87/Home-Assistant-ChronoTask/compare/v1.6.0-beta1...v1.7.0-beta1
